title: Operationalizing One Digital Health and FAIR Data Principles for Disease Surveillance in a Low-Medium Income Country in Africa: Qualitative Study in the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Recent crises involving zoonotic diseases (Ebola, COVID-19, and Mpox) have highlighted the limitations of fragmented public health systems for the prevention and response to health emergencies at the international and continental level, and particularly in Africa, more specifically in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC). In this context, the One Health (OH) approach and its extension, One Digital Health (ODH), articulated with the findable, accessible, interoperable, reusable (FAIR) principles, offer a framework for rethinking the digital transition in health in the DRC. This study analyzes the reality of this transition in Kinshasa, DRC, and questions the feasibility of ODH in this context. OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to (1) explore how stakeholders across human, animal, and environmental health sectors perceive and experience digital tool integration and data interoperability in Kinshasa; (2) identify structural, institutional, and technical constraints affecting cross-sectoral data sharing; and (3) analyze the sociotechnical conditions required for the operationalization of ODH in a fragmented digital health (DH) context. METHODS: A qualitative study was conducted in Kinshasa, DRC, between November 10, 2025, and November 25, 2025, combining semistructured interviews with key actors (health professionals, administrative officials, digital experts, and engaged citizens) and a document review of strategic and regulatory texts related to DH in the DRC. The data were analyzed using a thematic approach to identify the representations, uses, and constraints related to DH and the operationalization of ODH. RESULTS: Overall, 22 stakeholders participated (n=9, 40.9% human health; n=8, 36.4% animal health; n=4, 18.2% environmental health; n=1, 4.50% digital sector), predominantly male (n=15, 68.2%) and mainly in operational roles (n=12, 54.5%). Three interrelated topics emerged. First, a dual-track digital ecosystem characterized by the coexistence of formal platforms (eg, District Health Information Software 2 and electronic records) and informal tools (eg, WhatsApp [Meta]), with persistent paper-digital double-entry generating inefficiencies. Second, structural and governance bottlenecks, including electricity instability, limited connectivity, software incompatibility, external data-hosting concerns that affect sovereignty, and institutional silos that privilege human health over animal and environmental sectors. Third, prerequisites for operationalizing ODH emphasize foundational infrastructure (energy and internet), sustainable capacity building beyond one-off training, interoperable "bridges" between fragmented systems, and high-level political leadership. These elements were synthesized into an ODH-FAIR DRC conceptual model structured around three enabling pillars linking sectors for integrated zoonotic surveillance. CONCLUSIONS: Operationalizing ODH in DRC requires addressing foundational enablers beyond tools: synchronized energy-digital policies, decompartmentalized governance, and context-adapted capacity building. These insights inform low- and middle-income countries' DH strategies, urging donors and ministries to prioritize interoperability over isolated pilots to achieve sustainable zoonotic surveillance.

title_zh: 在非洲中低收入国家实施一种数字健康和公平疾病数据原则 监测:刚果民主共和国的定性研究。
source_body_en: BACKGROUND: Recent crises involving zoonotic diseases (Ebola, COVID-19, and Mpox) have highlighted the limitations of fragmented public health systems for the prevention and response to health emergencies at the international and continental level, and particularly in Africa, more specifically in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC). In this context, the One Health (OH) approach and its extension, One Digital Health (ODH), articulated with the findable, accessible, interoperable, reusable (FAIR) principles, offer a framework for rethinking the digital transition in health in the DRC. This study analyzes the reality of this transition in Kinshasa, DRC, and questions the feasibility of ODH in this context. OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to (1) explore how stakeholders across human, animal, and environmental health sectors perceive and experience digital tool integration and data interoperability in Kinshasa; (2) identify structural, institutional, and technical constraints affecting cross-sectoral data sharing; and (3) analyze the sociotechnical conditions required for the operationalization of ODH in a fragmented digital health (DH) context. METHODS: A qualitative study was conducted in Kinshasa, DRC, between November 10, 2025, and November 25, 2025, combining semistructured interviews with key actors (health professionals, administrative officials, digital experts, and engaged citizens) and a document review of strategic and regulatory texts related to DH in the DRC. The data were analyzed using a thematic approach to identify the representations, uses, and constraints related to DH and the operationalization of ODH. RESULTS: Overall, 22 stakeholders participated (n=9, 40.9% human health; n=8, 36.4% animal health; n=4, 18.2% environmental health; n=1, 4.50% digital sector), predominantly male (n=15, 68.2%) and mainly in operational roles (n=12, 54.5%). Three interrelated topics emerged. First, a dual-track digital ecosystem characterized by the coexistence of formal platforms (eg, District Health Information Software 2 and electronic records) and informal tools (eg, WhatsApp [Meta]), with persistent paper-digital double-entry generating inefficiencies. Second, structural and governance bottlenecks, including electricity instability, limited connectivity, software incompatibility, external data-hosting concerns that affect sovereignty, and institutional silos that privilege human health over animal and environmental sectors. Third, prerequisites for operationalizing ODH emphasize foundational infrastructure (energy and internet), sustainable capacity building beyond one-off training, interoperable "bridges" between fragmented systems, and high-level political leadership. These elements were synthesized into an ODH-FAIR DRC conceptual model structured around three enabling pillars linking sectors for integrated zoonotic surveillance. CONCLUSIONS: Operationalizing ODH in DRC requires addressing foundational enablers beyond tools: synchronized energy-digital policies, decompartmentalized governance, and context-adapted capacity building. These insights inform low- and middle-income countries' DH strategies, urging donors and ministries to prioritize interoperability over isolated pilots to achieve sustainable zoonotic surveillance.

title: Current Strategies for Selecting Recombinant Orthopoxvirus Proteins for Immunobiological and Diagnostic Applications
abstract: Orthopoxviruses are zoonotic DNA viruses of continuing public health importance, as highlighted by recent global mpox outbreaks. The high antigenic similarity among orthopoxviruses enables cross-reactive immune responses but complicates the development of serological diagnostic systems for serosurveillance, assessment of previous exposure, evaluation of vaccine-induced immunity, and species differentiation. This review summarizes current knowledge regarding the structure, biological functions, and diagnostic and vaccine potential of major orthopoxvirus recombinant antigens. Particular attention is given to the genomic organization of Orthopoxvirus, differences between intracellular mature virion (IMV) and extracellular enveloped virion (EV) forms, and the characteristics of key antigens, including A29, M1, H3, A35, and B6. Comparative phylogenetic analyses demonstrated a high degree of conservation among structurally important orthopoxvirus proteins while also identifying variable regions potentially relevant for differential diagnostics. Available evidence indicates that IMV-associated proteins are primarily involved in virus neutralization, whereas EV-associated antigens contribute mainly to limiting viral dissemination. Consequently, multicomponent antigen strategies combining IMV- and EV-associated proteins appear to provide the greatest potential for the development of effective serological assays and next-generation subunit vaccines. Overall, rational antigen selection should be based on integrated evaluation of structural, functional, and immunological properties to optimize orthopoxvirus diagnostic and vaccine platforms.

title_original: Current Strategies for Selecting Recombinant Orthopoxvirus Proteins for Immunobiological and Diagnostic Applications

analysis.scope_and_question: This review focuses on the selection of recombinant orthopoxvirus proteins for immunobiological and diagnostic applications, specifically addressing the Mpox virus and its clades. The central question is how to optimize the use of these proteins in developing effective diagnostic tools and vaccines.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is based on comparative phylogenetic analyses and integrates structural, functional, and immunological properties of key orthopoxvirus proteins. It does not explicitly report on databases, search dates, or meta-analysis methods.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review concludes that multicomponent antigen strategies combining IMV- and EV-associated proteins offer the greatest potential for effective serological assays and subunit vaccines. It highlights the importance of integrating structural, functional, and immunological properties for rational antigen selection.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review notes that while there is a high degree of conservation among structurally important orthopoxvirus proteins, there are variable regions that may be relevant for differential diagnostics. However, the evidence does not provide detailed information on the specific mechanisms or implications of these variable regions.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The review suggests that future research should focus on the development of multicomponent antigen strategies and the integration of structural, functional, and immunological data to optimize diagnostic and vaccine platforms for Mpox virus.

analysis.summary_en: This review explores the selection of recombinant orthopoxvirus proteins for immunobiological and diagnostic applications, emphasizing the importance of understanding the structural, functional, and immunological properties of key antigens such as A29, M1, H3, A35, and B6. It highlights the high antigenic similarity among orthopoxviruses, which complicates serological diagnostics but also supports cross-reactive immune responses. The review concludes that combining IMV- and EV-associated proteins in multicomponent strategies could enhance the effectiveness of serological assays and subunit vaccines. However, the evidence does not fully address the mechanisms or implications of variable regions identified in phylogenetic analyses. The study underscores the need for further research to refine antigen selection and improve diagnostic and vaccine platforms for Mpox virus.

abstract_zh: 正如最近的全球 猴痘 暴发 所强调的那样,正痘病毒 是人畜共患 DNA 病毒,对公共卫生具有持续重要性。正痘病毒 之间的高抗原相似性使得 免疫应答 能够发生交叉反应,但使用于血清监测、评估既往暴露、评估 疫苗 诱导的免疫和物种分化的血清学诊断系统的开发变得复杂。本综述总结了有关主要 正痘病毒 重组抗原的结构、生物学功能以及诊断和 疫苗 潜力的当前知识。特别关注 正痘病毒 的基因组组织、细胞内成熟病毒颗粒 (IMV) 和细胞外有包膜病毒颗粒 (EV) 形式之间的差异,以及关键抗原的特征,包括 A29、M1、H3、A35 和 B6。比较系统发育分析表明,结构重要的 正痘病毒 蛋白之间具有高度保守性,同时还鉴定了可能与鉴别诊断相关的可变区域。现有证据表明,IMV 相关蛋白主要参与病毒中和,而 EV 相关抗原主要有助于限制病毒传播。因此,结合 IMV 和 EV 相关蛋白的多组分抗原策略似乎为开发有效的血清学检测和下一代亚基 疫苗 提供了最大的潜力。总体而言,合理的抗原选择应基于结构、功能和免疫学特性的综合评估,以优化正痘病毒诊断和疫苗平台。

title: Dynamics of Orthopoxvirus Stability Under Simulated Luminal Conditions of the Gastrointestinal Tract for Assessing the Feasibility of Oral Immunization
abstract: Background/Objectives: Mpox (formerly monkeypox) is a re-emerging global health threat. While current vaccines are injectable, oral vaccination offers a painless alternative, though the harsh gastrointestinal (GI) environment challenges live viral vaccines. This study evaluated the stability of orthopoxviruses under simulated GI conditions to assess the physicochemical feasibility of oral mpox immunization. Methods: Attenuated and virulent strains of vaccinia, cowpox, and camelpox viruses were exposed to simulated gastric (pH 1.0–2.0 and 3.0–4.0 with pepsin) and intestinal (pH 7.0–7.5) conditions at 37 °C for 180 min. Viral titers were determined via cell culture assays. The physicochemical protective efficacy of enteric-coated capsules was evaluated using standard dissolution testing parameters. Results: All orthopoxviruses were rapidly inactivated under highly acidic fasting conditions (pH 1.0–2.0). However, they exhibited high stability at pH 3.0–4.0 and 7.0–7.5, retaining approximately 20–30% of their initial infectivity after 180 min. Enteric-coated capsules successfully maintained shell integrity in simulated gastric fluids for over 3 h and dissolved completely under intestinal conditions within ~130 min, aligning with small intestine transit times. Conclusions: Orthopoxviruses possess sufficient intestinal stability to support the physicochemical feasibility of oral immunization, provided they are protected from gastric acidity. Enteric-coated capsules represent a highly suitable delivery system for the intestinal release of live orthopoxvirus-based candidates, warranting further in vivo preclinical evaluation.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在评估正痘病毒在模拟胃肠道条件下的稳定性,以评估口服免疫猴痘的可行性。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究将牛痘、牛痘和骆驼痘病毒的减毒毒株暴露在 37°C 的模拟胃和肠道条件下 180 分钟。
elements_zh.methods: 通过细胞培养测定测定病毒滴度,并使用标准溶出测试参数评估肠溶胶囊的理化保护功效。
elements_zh.main_results: 所有 正痘病毒 在高酸性禁食条件下(pH 1.0-2.0)均迅速失活,但在 pH 3.0-4.0 和 7.0-7.5 下表现出高稳定性,180 分钟后保留了约 20-30% 的初始感染性。肠溶胶囊在模拟胃液中成功保持壳完整性超过 3 小时,并在肠道条件下在约 130 分钟内完全溶解。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者得出的结论是,正痘病毒 具有足够的肠道稳定性,以支持口服免疫的理化可行性,前提是它们免受胃酸的影响。肠溶胶囊被认为是非常适合基于 正痘病毒 的活体 疫苗 的递送系统。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,通过适当的保护措施,针对 猴痘 的口服免疫是可行的,这可能会导致非侵入性 疫苗 递送系统的开发。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究是在模拟条件下进行的,没有考虑体内的复杂性,这可能会影响结果的普遍性。由于数据仅具有抽象性质,证据的强度中等。

abstract_zh: 背景/目标:猴痘(以前称为猴痘)是一种重新出现的全球健康威胁。虽然目前的 疫苗 是可注射的,但口服 疫苗 提供了一种无痛替代方案,尽管恶劣的胃肠 (GI) 环境对活病毒 疫苗 提出了挑战。本研究评估了 正痘病毒 在模拟胃肠道条件下的稳定性,以评估口服 猴痘 免疫的理化可行性。方法:将牛痘、牛痘和骆驼痘病毒的减毒毒株暴露于 37°C 的模拟胃(pH 1.0-2.0 和 3.0-4.0,胃蛋白酶)和肠道(pH 7.0-7.5)条件下 180 分钟。通过细胞培养测定确定病毒滴度。使用标准溶出测试参数评估肠溶胶囊的理化保护功效。结果:所有 正痘病毒 在高酸性禁食条件下(pH 1.0-2.0)迅速失活。然而,它们在 pH 3.0-4.0 和 7.0-7.5 下表现出高度稳定性,180 分钟后保留了约 20-30% 的初始感染性。肠溶胶囊在模拟胃液中成功保持壳完整性超过 3 小时,并在肠道条件下在约 130 分钟内完全溶解,与小肠转运时间一致。结论:正痘病毒 具有足够的肠道稳定性,以支持口服免疫的理化可行性,前提是它们免受胃酸的影响。肠溶胶囊代表了一种非常适合肠道释放活体 正痘病毒 候选药物的递送系统,值得进一步的体内临床前评估。

analysis_zh.main_results: 所有 正痘病毒 在高酸性禁食条件下(pH 1.0-2.0)均迅速失活,但在 pH 3.0-4.0 和 7.0-7.5 下表现出高稳定性,180 分钟后保留了约 20-30% 的初始感染性。肠溶胶囊在模拟胃液中成功保持壳完整性超过 3 小时,并在肠道条件下在约 130 分钟内完全溶解。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者得出的结论是,正痘病毒 具有足够的肠道稳定性,以支持口服免疫的理化可行性,前提是它们免受胃酸的影响。肠溶胶囊被认为是非常适合基于 正痘病毒 的活体 疫苗 的递送系统。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,通过适当的保护措施,针对 猴痘 的口服免疫是可行的,这可能会导致非侵入性 疫苗 递送系统的开发。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究是在模拟条件下进行的,没有考虑体内的复杂性,这可能会影响结果的普遍性。由于数据仅具有抽象性质,证据的强度中等。
